title: River Life Operating System Product Presentation and Public Launch Path
purpose: Define and implement the governed customer-facing presentation and public launch path for The River Life Operating System only after PRODUCT-001E end-to-end commerce readiness has been demonstrated, while preserving the approved release, verified payment, canonical order, fulfillment idempotency, privacy, security, and private-source boundaries established by prior PRODUCT-001 phases.
governingPrinciples: Public presentation is a separate governance concern from technical commerce readiness.
A technically functional checkout must not become publicly discoverable or customer-usable until PRODUCT-001F explicitly advances the publication boundary.
The working product price is not publication authority.
Public availability must be deliberate rather than inferred from the existence of product, checkout, fulfillment, or delivery code.
The customer-facing product presentation must accurately describe the actual V1 product and may not promise capabilities, outcomes, services, or proof that do not exist.
The paid value proposition must remain structured application and guided execution rather than merely republishing freely available River essays.
Product presentation must remain consistent with the source-grounded PRODUCT-001 curriculum and completed V1 artifact.
The approved release requirement remains authoritative.
Verified provider payment remains required before fulfillment.
Canonical River order identity remains authoritative.
The private source manuscript boundary remains authoritative.
No customer commerce data may enter public static content.
No provider secret, webhook secret, transactional-email secret, private artifact identity, or internal repository path may enter browser-delivered content.
Launch authorization must be explicit and must not be inferred merely because all implementation tests pass.
Public launch must be reversible without corrupting existing order, entitlement, fulfillment, or delivery state.

requiredCustomerFacingElements: accurate description of the V1 outcome
price only when price publication is authorized
availability only when availability publication is authorized
purchase call to action only when checkout publication and customer purchase are authorized
presentationContract.customerDeliverable: The approved River Life Operating System v1 digital PDF release delivered through the governed transactional fulfillment path.
prohibitedPresentation: claims that the product includes capabilities deferred by PRODUCT-001D or PRODUCT-001E

requirements: The River website remains the authoritative customer-facing presentation surface.
Product presentation must use River-owned page structure and visual language rather than delegating product identity to the payment provider.
Stripe may own secure payment collection but must not become the product presentation authority.
Customer-facing checkout initiation must originate from a governed River-owned launch surface.
Success and cancellation states must return customers to River-owned website paths.
No permanent unauthenticated paid artifact URL may be exposed.

publicationState.rule: Each publication capability remains closed until the corresponding PRODUCT-001F implementation and launch-readiness gates explicitly advance it. Creating this specification does not itself authorize publication.

publicationAdvancementRules: Price may be presented publicly only after the presentation contract and price-display implementation pass their governed validation.
Availability may be presented publicly only after customer-facing delivery expectations and launch-state behavior are validated.
Checkout may be exposed publicly only after the purchase CTA points to the already-verified governed checkout mechanism.

Customer purchase may be authorized only after the complete public path from presentation through checkout, verified payment, persistence, fulfillment, and recorded delivery is represented and validated.
Public launch may be authorized only after final PRODUCT-001F launch-readiness verification.
No individual implementation slice may silently flip a later publication authorization.

implementationSequence.name: Public presentation contract and launch-state foundation
implementationSequence.outcome: Customer-facing product presentation requirements, launch-state boundaries, and explicit publication authorization states exist in code or governed configuration without exposing commerce publicly.

implementationSequence.name: River Life Operating System product presentation
implementationSequence.outcome: The River-owned website contains an accurate customer-facing presentation of the V1 product, its purpose, five-part architecture, deliverable, boundaries, and value without yet exposing unauthorized purchase capability.

implementationSequence.name: Public price and availability presentation
implementationSequence.outcome: The governed  V1 price and product availability can be represented accurately on River-owned presentation surfaces only after their publication gates are deliberately advanced.

implementationSequence.name: Customer-facing purchase call to action
implementationSequence.outcome: A governed River-owned purchase CTA can initiate the already-verified Stripe Checkout path without moving payment correctness or fulfillment authority into browser-delivered code.

implementationSequence.name: Customer launch-path integration
implementationSequence.outcome: Presentation, price, availability, checkout initiation, success and cancellation return paths, and customer-facing delivery expectations operate as one coherent launch path while preserving all PRODUCT-001D and PRODUCT-001E boundaries.

implementationSequence.name: Public launch readiness gate
implementationSequence.outcome: Public product launch may be authorized only after the complete customer-facing path is validated against presentation accuracy, publication authority, commerce readiness, fulfillment correctness, security, privacy, and reversibility requirements.

completionCriteria: A governed customer-facing presentation contract exists.
The five-part River Life Operating System architecture is accurately represented.
The customer deliverable is described accurately.
Paid value is represented as structured application and guided execution rather than simple republication of free essays.
No unsupported testimonials, audience proof, customer results, professional authority, or guaranteed outcomes are introduced.
Price publication occurs only through explicit PRODUCT-001F authority.
Availability publication occurs only through explicit PRODUCT-001F authority.
Checkout publication occurs only through explicit PRODUCT-001F authority.
Customer purchase authorization occurs only through explicit PRODUCT-001F authority.
The public purchase CTA uses the existing governed checkout mechanism rather than creating a second commerce path.
The complete customer path preserves verified payment, canonical order, approved release, entitlement, fulfillment, delivery, idempotency, privacy, and security boundaries.
The paid artifact remains private except through governed fulfillment.
Repository validation passes for every PRODUCT-001F implementation slice.
Final public launch authorization occurs only through PRODUCT-001F-06.
